source_user: An agent repeatedly calls a calculator when the answer is already known. Design metrics and an intervention. Scenario variant 34: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure unnecessary calls, tool success, final correctness, trajectory length, tool latency, and recovery; add a stop/no-tool evaluation and preference or reward signal.
corrected_answer: For scenario variant 34, assume the calculator is available, model and policy versions are pinned, tool traces can be logged with privacy minimization, and final answers can be independently judged. Define an unnecessary call as a calculator invocation for which the request is answerable correctly without external arithmetic under the stated precision and ambiguity; do not label calls unnecessary when exact precision, a long or error-prone computation, missing information, or verification is required. Log task class and difficulty, model/policy version, gate decision and rationale, call count, expression, result or error, tool and end-to-end wall-clock latency in milliseconds, tokens/cost, final correctness, abstention, retries, and recovery. Report unnecessary-call rate, tool success and error rate, final correctness, trajectory length, p50/p95/p99 latency, cost, abstention, and recovery, stratified by task class and difficulty with confidence intervals. Falsifiable hypothesis: on a locked held-out set, a stop/no-tool gate lowers unnecessary-call rate by at least 30% and p95 end-to-end latency by at least 10% while final correctness is non-inferior within 1 percentage point; if any preregistered criterion fails, do not ship. Randomize matched requests between the current policy and the gate, tune only on disjoint development data, and use paired bootstrap intervals plus a preregistered non-inferiority test. Include both easy no-tool cases and precision-sensitive, ambiguous, and tool-failure cases; inspect calls incorrectly suppressed and calls retained unnecessarily. Use preference or reward shaping only with separate correctness/tool-necessity labels, because rewarding abstention alone can induce unsafe under-use. Control for request mix, difficulty, model version, cache, concurrency, hardware, network/tool load, prompt changes, and evaluator drift. Store only redacted/minimal traces, restrict access, and do not expose sensitive expressions or results. Canary the gate with hard safety and correctness floors, rate limits, monitoring, and a kill switch; roll back on correctness regression, elevated recovery/error rate, tail-latency harm, distribution shift, or privacy incident. These are provisional engineering criteria and require domain-expert review.
